LESSON: INTERDEPENDENCE OF PEOPLE

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Population
Topic 2.1: Interdependence of people

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Interdependence of people. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do people in the county depend on each other?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify ways in which people depend on each other in the county
2. explain the benefits of interdependence of people in the county
3. use chart to illustrate the benefits of interdependence people
4. appreciate the interdependence of people in the County

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INTERDEPENDENCE OF PEOPLE
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Interdependence of people helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: INTERDEPENDENCE OF PEOPLE
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify ways in which people depend on each other in the county

What this means
In this part you learn to identify ways in which people depend on each other in the county. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify ways in which people depend on each other in the county.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Interdependence of people” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify ways in which people depend on each other in the county. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the benefits of interdependence of people in the county

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the benefits of interdependence of people in the county. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the benefits of interdependence of people in the county.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Interdependence of people.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the benefits of interdependence of people in the county. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use chart to illustrate the benefits of interdependence people

What this means
In this part you learn to use chart to illustrate the benefits of interdependence people. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use chart to illustrate the benefits of interdependence people.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use chart to illustrate the benefits of interdependence people. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the interdependence of people in the County

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the interdependence of people in the County. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the interdependence of people in the County.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Interdependence of people” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the interdependence of people in the County. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Interdependence of people is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Interdependence of people” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify ways in which people depend on each other in the county)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Interdependence of people. (skill: explain the benefits of interdependence of people in the county)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: use chart to illustrate the benefits of interdependence people)

Example 4: Connect “Interdependence of people” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: appreciate the interdependence of people in the County)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Interdependence of people to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify ways in which people depend on each other in the county.
3. Practise this skill: explain the benefits of interdependence of people in the county.
4. Practise this skill: use chart to illustrate the benefits of interdependence people.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Interdependence of people from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Interdependence of people: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Interdependence of people?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do people in the county depend on each other?
2. Why should we support each other in the county?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Interdependence of people means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify ways in which people depend on each other in the county.
5. Be able to: explain the benefits of interdependence of people in the county.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
